transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you. Well, I guess what finally scared me into coming in is that I just keep making these really dumb technical mistakes at work. I'm a camera operator and video editor, and I'm making errors I absolutely know better than to make. 

Like, I'll label camera cards wrong, or I'll completely miss a timecode note. Or I'll export a client cut with the wrong lower-third graphic, even after I swear I've already checked it. It's just getting really frustrating and I need to figure out what's going on.
Have you struggled with these kinds of attention and detail mistakes throughout your life, including as a child, or is this a recent change?

It's definitely not recent. It's been an issue my whole life, really. Even back in elementary school, my teachers were always moving my desk around because I just couldn't stay in my seat. I was always getting up, or I'd just blurt out answers, or I'd be bothering my classmates before I even realized I was doing it. So, yeah, it's been a lifelong thing.
As an adult, do you still often feel restless or have a hard time sitting still when you are expected to?

Yeah, I do. It's definitely still a problem. 

For example, when I have to sit still through a client screening... it honestly feels like there's this pressure building up under my skin. I just get this overwhelming feeling that I need to get up and do something with my body, even when I know I’m supposed to just sit there and watch the cut quietly. It's really uncomfortable.
